text:
`python3 -m unittest` now passes all 25 tests. I didn't touch the tests. There were seven bugs, all in `taskflow/`:

| File | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `queue.py` | `_Entry.sort_key` returned `(seq, -priority)`, so insertion order won over priority. | It now returns `(-priority, seq)`. |
| `retry.py` | `should_retry` used `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1`, so the last permitted attempt was never made. | It now uses `attempts_made < max_attempts`. |
| `events.py` | `_prefix_matches` had the arguments reversed (`prefix.startswith(topic + ".")`), so prefix subscribers never matched. | It now checks `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`. |
| `statemachine.py` | `batch_order_ok` used `>=`, but the batch invariant is non-increasing priority. That wrongly rejected a lower-priority task after a higher one, and the scheduler then marked the rejected task `FAILED`. | It now uses `<=`. |
| `resources.py` | `ResourcePool.release` did `used -= 1` instead of `used -= cost`, so multi-unit costs leaked capacity. | It now subtracts `cost`. |
| `config.py` | `deep_merge` recursed as `deep_merge(value, result[key])`, which swapped the arguments so defaults overrode the task's own settings. | It now calls `deep_merge(result[key], value)`. |
| `scheduler.py` | `_cascade_skip` used `dag.dependents` (direct children only), so grandchildren stayed `PENDING`. | It now uses `dag.transitive_dependents`. |

Most of the 18 original failures came from a handful of these bugs. The resource-pool leak, the retry boundary and the priority ordering each broke several pipeline tests.
